1.1: These the words of Jeremiah, son of Hilkiah—one of the priests from a lil' town called Anathoth, out in Benjamin's territory.
1.2: The word of the Lord came to him back when Josiah, son of Amon, was king of Judah—in the 13th year of his reign.
1.3: God kept speakin' to him during the time of Jehoiakim (Josiah's son), all the way until Zedekiah (also Josiah's son) was king. That's when Jerusalem got taken over in the fifth month.
1.4: Then God pulled up on me and said:
1.5: "Before I even formed you in your mama's belly, I knew you. Before you took your first breath, I had already set you apart. I chose you to speak to nations."
1.6: I said, "Lord God… I don't know how to speak like that—I'm just a kid!"
1.7: But God said, "Don't say you too young. You gon' go wherever I send you and say whatever I tell you to."
1.8: "Don't be scared of folks, 'cause I'm with you. I got you," says the Lord.
1.9: Then God reached out, touched my mouth, and said, "Look—I just put My words in your mouth."
1.10: "Today, I'm putting you in position. You got authority over nations and kingdoms—To rip out and tear down, To destroy and demolish, To rebuild and replant."
1.11: Then God asked me, "Jeremiah, what you seein'?" I said, "I see a almond branch."
1.12: God said, "Good eye. You seein' right. I'm watchin' close to make sure My word come true."
1.13: God came back a second time: "What you see now?" I said, "I see a pot boilin' over, tilted from the north."
1.14: Then the Lord said: "Trouble comin' from the north—about to spill out over the whole land."
1.15: "I'm callin' all them northern kingdoms to roll up. They gon' set up right at Jerusalem's gates, pressin' against her walls and all Judah's cities."
1.16: "I'm about to lay down judgment for all the wrong they been doin'—turnin' they back on Me, burnin' incense to fake gods, and worshippin' what they hands built."
1.17: "So get up, get dressed, and speak every word I give you. Don't let fear shake you, or I'ma shake you up in front of them."
1.18: "Today I made you strong—like a fortified city, an iron pillar, and bronze walls. You standin' against kings, officials, priests, and all the people."
1.19: "They gon' come at you—but they won't win. I'm with you," says the Lord, "I'm the One deliverin' you."

2.1: Then God spoke to me again, sayin'—
2.2: "Go speak loud in Jerusalem so everybody hear: I remember you. How sweet you used to be, How you loved Me like we was engaged. You followed Me through that dry wilderness, Even when the land ain't have nothin'."
2.3: "Israel was holy to Me—My first pick. Anybody who messed with them? They brought trouble on they own heads."
2.4: Listen up, y'all—whole house of Jacob, all the fams in Israel:
2.5: God say: "What did I do wrong to your ancestors? Why'd they dip on Me? Started chasin' worthless idols, And turned into nothin' theyself."
2.6: "They ain't even ask, 'Where's the Lord?' The One who brought us outta Egypt, Led us through them deserts, Through all that dry land, danger, and death— Places nobody dared to live."
2.7: "I brought y'all into a land full of blessings, Fruitful and rich. But soon as y'all touched it, You trashed it. Defiled what I gave you."
2.8: "The priests ain't call out for Me. The law folks didn't even know Me. Leaders rebelled. Prophets out here speakin' on Baal's behalf, Chasin' nonsense that don't help nobody."
2.9: "So yeah—I got beef with y'all," says the Lord. "And I'ma keep bringin' this case against you—and your grandkids too."
2.10: "Look out past Cyprus. Peep Kedar in the desert. See if any other nation switched out their gods— Even if they fake!"
2.11: "But My people? They swapped out their glory for garbage."
2.12: "Even the heavens shook they head. Y'all got creation itself confused and scared."
2.13: "They did Me dirty two ways: 1. Walked away from Me—the source of livin' water. 2. Tried to dig they own wells—cracked ones that can't even hold no water."
2.14: "Is Israel just some house slave? Somebody born to be used? Why he always gettin' ran through?"
2.15: "Lions roared on him. Tore his land up. Burned his cities to the ground. Ain't nobody livin' there no more."
2.16: "Noph and Tahpanhes? Them Egyptians busted y'all crown—took y'all pride."
2.17: "And why? 'Cause you turned your back on Me When I was tryna guide you."
2.18: "Now you out here beggin' Egypt for help, Drankin' from their rivers. Or runnin' to Assyria tryna sip from theirs. Why you keep flirtin' with bondage?"
2.19: "Your own mess is catchin' up with you. Your wrong turns clappin' back. You gon' see—leavin' Me was a bad and bitter move. Ain't no fear of Me left in you," says the Lord God of Heaven's armies.
2.20: "I already freed you—broke your chains. You promised, 'I won't wild out again.' But next thing I know, You up under every shady tree, Actin' like you don't know Me. Bein' fast."
2.21: "I planted you like premium seed—top quality vine. How'd you turn into some wild, raggedy off-brand?"
2.22: "You could scrub all day with bleach and lye, But your sins still loud and clear to Me," says the Lord God.
2.23: "How you gon' say, 'I ain't did nothin'? 'I ain't chase no fake gods'? Look at your trail. You movin' reckless—like a wild camel runnin' loose."
2.24: "Like a donkey in heat, sniffin' the wind for attention. Ain't nobody gotta chase her—she out here findin' them."
2.25: "I tried to warn you— Told you to slow down, rest, protect yourself. But you said, 'Ain't no hope for me. I'm too deep in this—I love these foreign gods, And I ain't lettin' go.'"
2.26: "Just like a thief feel shame when they caught— That's how Israel feel now. Them, their kings, their officials, their priests, and their prophets too."
2.27: "They out here tellin' a tree, 'You my daddy,' And a stone, 'You gave me life.' Turned their backs on Me, But soon as trouble hits: 'God, come save us!'"
2.28: "Where them gods you made now? Tell them to pull up and save you. You got gods in every city—but none of 'em show up when it counts."
2.29: "Why you even arguing with Me? Y'all all been disobedient," says the Lord.
2.30: "I tried disciplining your kids—but they ain't listen. Y'all even killed the prophets I sent. Tore them up like wild lions."
2.31: "Y'all better recognize My word! Was I ever a dry place to y'all? Was I darkness and confusion? So why y'all actin' like y'all runnin' things, Sayin', 'We don't need You no more'?"
2.32: "Can a bride forget her wedding dress? Can a young woman forget her jewelry? But My people? They forgot Me for days on end—like I ain't never done nothin' for them."
2.33: "You even learned how to make your wild behavior look cute— Taught the worst of women how to do what you do."
2.34: "And I ain't even had to dig deep— Your clothes got innocent blood on them. You out here killin' the poor and actin' like it ain't happen."
2.35: "Still, you say, 'I'm innocent. God's anger ain't gon' last.' But I'm comin' for you— 'Cause you keep sayin', 'I ain't did nothin.'"
2.36: "Why you jumpin' from one scheme to the next? Tryna switch up your alliances? You gon' be just as ashamed of Egypt As you was when Assyria let you down."
2.37: "You gon' walk away from them lookin' defeated— Hands on your head, stressed. 'Cause the Lord already rejected them folks you trusted. They not gon' save you."

3.1: "They say if a man divorces his wife, And she run off, marry somebody else— Can he take her back? Ain't that land already messed up?" God say, "But you? You been out here with all kinds of lovers… And I'm still sayin', come back to Me."
3.2: "Look around—high places, empty roads— Where haven't you laid down? You was waitin' for them like a desert bandit, Pollutin' the land with your reckless ways."
3.3: "That's why the rain stopped. The sky been holdin' back. You walkin' around bold-faced like it ain't nothin', Ain't even tryna be ashamed."
3.4: "Ain't you gon' cry out to Me now? 'My Father, the One who raised me up right.'"
3.5: "You really think I'm just gon' stay mad forever? You talk real sweet, but your actions been off. You doin' dirt every chance you get."
3.6: Then God said to me while Josiah was king: "Did you see what Israel did? She ran up every mountain, Under every shady tree—wildin' out."
3.7: "I told her, 'Come back to Me.' She said no. And her sister Judah saw it all."
3.8: "I divorced Israel for all that spiritual cheatin', Gave her the papers. But Judah? She ain't even flinch. She went and acted just as bad."
3.9: "Judah made it casual—like it was no big deal. She even started messin' with trees and rocks like they was gods."
3.10: "And even with all that, Judah didn't come back with her heart. She just put on a show," says the Lord.
3.11: Then the Lord said: "Backslidin' Israel actin' more right Than fake-hearted Judah."
3.12: "So go north and tell 'em: Come home, Israel," says the Lord. "I ain't gon' stay mad. I'm merciful. I ain't built to stay angry."
3.13: "Just own up to it. Admit you crossed Me. You ran off after other gods And stopped listenin' to Me."
3.14: "Come back, My rebellious kids," says the Lord. "I'm still married to you. I'll take one from a city, two from a fam, And bring y'all back to Zion."
3.15: "I'ma give y'all real shepherds—leaders that got My heart. They gon' feed you knowledge and understanding."
3.16: "When y'all grow and flourish in the land again," says the Lord, "You won't even talk about the Ark of the Covenant no more. Ain't gon' think about it, miss it, or try to rebuild it."
3.17: "Back then, Jerusalem gon' be called 'The Lord's Throne.' Nations gon' pull up there, And folks ain't gon' follow their messed-up hearts no more."
3.18: "In those days, Judah and Israel gon' walk together again, Returnin' from the north, Back to the land I gave their ancestors."
3.19: "I been tryna treat y'all like My own kids, Give y'all a sweet inheritance— A beautiful land among the nations. I wanted you to call Me 'Father' And never turn away."
3.20: "But like a wife who sneaks out on her husband, That's how Israel did Me dirty," says the Lord.
3.21: There's a voice cryin' out in the hills— Weepin', beggin'. It's Israel's kids, Realizin' they went the wrong way And forgot their God.
3.22: "Come back, rebellious ones, And I'll heal all that backslidin'." Then they say: "We comin' to You— You really are the Lord our God."
3.23: "Them high hills and mountaintop altars? They ain't never saved nobody. Only in the Lord do we find salvation."
3.24: "Our shame ate up everything— Our parents' work, our animals, Even our sons and daughters."
3.25: "We layin' down in our shame, Covered in guilt. 'Cause we sinned against the Lord— Us and our people, From way back to right now. We just ain't listened to His voice."

4.1: "If you really gon' come back, Israel," says the Lord, "Then come back to Me. Cut out all that fake god worship— Put it away where I can't see it, Then you'll be solid."
4.2: "You gon' swear by My name and mean it this time— Sayin', 'The Lord lives,' With truth, with justice, with righteousness. Then even other nations gon' wanna be blessed through Me."
4.3: This what God tellin' the people of Judah and Jerusalem: "Break up that hard ground in your heart. Stop tryin' to plant seeds in thorny mess."
4.4: "Y'all need to circumcise your hearts. Yeah, I said hearts—not just bodies. Cut away that stubbornness, Before My anger blaze out like a wildfire— Unstoppable, All 'cause of your wicked ways."
4.5: Let Judah know. Blast it in Jerusalem: "Sound the trumpet! Tell everybody: Fall back! Head for the fortified cities!"
4.6: "Put the signal up toward Zion. Run for cover—don't wait around! I'm bringin' disaster from the north. It's gon' hit hard."
4.7: "That lion done left his cave. The nation destroyer is on the move. He comin' to wreck your land, Tear up your cities— Ain't gon' be nobody left in 'em."
4.8: "Y'all better throw on that sackcloth, Cry out loud. God's wrath ain't lettin' up."
4.9: "That day," says the Lord, "Even kings gon' lose heart, Leaders gon' be shook, Priests confused, And prophets stunned."
4.10: I said, "Lord God… You really let these folks believe they was safe, Like peace was on the way— But the sword done cut deep."
4.11: A dry, scorching wind gon' blow in From the desolate hills. It ain't no breeze for cleanin' or coolin' down—
4.12: This wind's too strong. It's a storm of judgment— God's own verdict blowin' through.
4.13: "The enemy ridin' in like storm clouds, Whippin' up whirlwinds with chariots. Their horses faster than eagles." We finished. We been robbed.
4.14: "Jerusalem—wash your heart clean! That's the only way to get saved. How long you gon' keep them evil thoughts Rentin' space in your mind?"
4.15: A voice shoutin' from Dan, Trouble comin' down from Ephraim.
4.16: "Tell the whole world— Judgment is comin' for Jerusalem. Enemies posted like guards, Surroundin' the city— 'Cause she went rogue against Me," says the Lord.
4.17: "They settin' up shop like watchmen in the fields, 'Cause y'all crossed Me."
4.18: "You brought this on yourself. Your own actions caused this pain. It's your mess— Bitter and deep, Right down to the heart."
4.19: Ohhh my soul! My chest hurt bad! My heart beatin' crazy— I can't keep quiet! I hear the trumpet. I hear the war cry.
4.20: It's back-to-back destruction! The whole land gettin' ripped apart. One minute I got tents, Next minute they snatched. My shelter—gone in a blink.
4.21: How long I gotta watch this warning flag wave? How long I gotta hear that trumpet?
4.22: "My people so foolish," God says. "They don't know Me. They actin' like little kids with no sense. They smart when it comes to doin' wrong— But good? They clueless."
4.23: I looked at the earth— It was empty, chaotic. The sky? Dark and blank.
4.24: I looked at the mountains— They was shakin'. Even the hills was doin' the Harlem shake.
4.25: I looked— Ain't nobody around. Even the birds flew off.
4.26: The land, once fruitful, was straight-up wilderness. Cities? Destroyed. God's anger was heavy.
4.27: "The land gon' be wrecked," says the Lord. "But I ain't wiping everything out."
4.28: "The whole earth gon' grieve. The sky gon' go dark— 'Cause I said what I said. This judgment? Locked in. I ain't takin' it back."
4.29: When the enemy comes with their horses and bows, Everybody gon' dip— Hide in bushes, climb rocks. Every city left empty. No soul in sight.
4.30: "So when you get stripped of everything, What you gon' do then? Dress yourself up in red, Wear gold, beat your face— But it's all a waste. Your lovers gon' turn on you. They out to kill you now."
4.31: I hear the cries of a woman in labor— Her first child, Her first pain. It's Zion's daughter, Cryin' with her hands stretched out, sayin': 'I'm done. I'm tired. Murderers all around me.'"

5.1: "Run up and down Jerusalem's streets. Look around. See if you can find one person—just one— Who stands on justice, who loves the truth. If you find one, I'll let the whole city slide."
5.2: "They say, 'As sure as the Lord lives,' But they lyin'. Ain't no truth in that."
5.3: Lord, ain't You watchin' for truth? You tried to check them— But they ain't even flinch. You burned off the nonsense— But they still act brand new. They got faces hard like stone, Refusin' to turn back.
5.4: So I said, "Maybe it's just the broke folks. They don't know no better. They ain't been taught God's way."
5.5: "Let me talk to the big dogs—leaders and wise folks. Surely they know better." But nah—they broke loose too. Snapped God's commands like twigs.
5.6: So now, lions from the woods gon' tear 'em up, Desert wolves gon' pounce, Leopards watchin' their streets. Step outside? You finished. All 'cause they done piled up sin on sin, Backslide after backslide.
5.7: "So tell Me—how I'm supposed to forgive this? Your kids turned they back on Me, Swearin' on fake gods. I fed 'em till they full— And they repaid Me by creepin' to the brothel."
5.8: "They actin' like wild stallions in heat, Neighin' after their neighbor's wife."
5.9: "You think I ain't gon' check 'em for this?" says the Lord. "You think I ain't gon' handle a whole nation actin' like this?"
5.10: "Go up to their city walls—tear some stuff down. But don't destroy it all. Trim the branches. Those folks don't even belong to Me no more."
5.11: "Both Israel and Judah been shady," says the Lord. "They two-timin' Me."
5.12: "They straight up lied on Me, sayin', 'God ain't really doin' all that. We ain't gon' see no trouble— No sword, no famine.'"
5.13: "Now the prophets? Just blowin' hot air. Ain't no Word in 'em. They just talkin'. They gon' get what they deserve."
5.14: So God said, "Since they said all that, I'ma make My words in your mouth like fire— And this people? Like wood. It's gon' burn them up."
5.15: "Listen, Israel: I'ma bring a nation from far off," says the Lord. "They strong. They old. They speak a language you don't understand."
5.16: "Their arrows like open graves— They soldiers don't miss."
5.17: "They gon' eat your harvest, your bread, What your kids supposed to eat. They takin' your animals, your vineyards, your fig trees. They gon' wreck the cities y'all trust in—with the sword."
5.18: "But even then," says the Lord, "I ain't gon' wipe y'all out completely."
5.19: "When y'all finally ask, 'Why God doin' this to us?' Tell 'em: 'Same way y'all left Him to serve other gods— Now y'all gon' serve foreigners in a land that ain't yours.'"
5.20: Announce this in Jacob's house, Preach it in Judah:
5.21: "Y'all foolish and clueless. Got eyes—but don't see. Got ears—but don't hear."
5.22: "Ain't you scared of Me?" says the Lord. "I'm the One who told the ocean, 'This far and no more.' Waves crash all they want— But they can't cross My boundary."
5.23: "But y'all? Y'all got rebellious hearts— Hardheaded and gone."
5.24: "Ain't nobody sayin', 'Let's fear God— He the One sendin' the rains, The One keepin' the seasons goin, Bringin' the harvest on time.'"
5.25: "Y'all sins blocked all that. That's why good things ain't reachin' you."
5.26: "My own people got snakes among 'em. Liars settin' traps, Catchin' folks like hunters catch birds."
5.27: "Their houses full of dirty deals— Like cages full of birds. That's how they got rich."
5.28: "They fat with greed, Outdo even the worst evildoers. They ain't fightin' for the orphans. They ain't helpin' the poor. But they still stay winnin'? Nah."
5.29: "You think I ain't gon' check that?" says the Lord. "You think I ain't gon' step in on a nation this foul?"
5.30: "Something wild and evil Happening in the land—"
5.31: "The prophets out here lyin'. The priests runnin' the show off vibes. And the people? They love it like that." "But what y'all gon' do when it all crashes down?"

6.1: Yo, children of Benjamin, y'all better dip—get outta Jerusalem! Blow the trumpet down in Tekoa, light that signal fire in Beth Haccerem. Trouble comin' from the north, and it's gon' be bad.
6.2: I pictured Zion like a beautiful, delicate woman—now look at her.
6.3: The shepherds gon' roll up with they flocks, settin' up tents all around her. Everybody takin' what's theirs.
6.4: They say, "Time to go to war. Let's hit her at noon." But then they panic—"The day's almost gone, shadows creepin'. We waited too long!"
6.5: "Nah, let's go at night then. We takin' her down, palaces and all."
6.6: The Lord of Heaven's Armies said: "Cut down some trees. Build up that siege ramp. This city 'bout to get it—it's full of straight-up evil.
6.7: Just like a fountain bubbles up with water, Jerusalem overflowin' with wickedness. Violence, robbery, cries and pain—they never stop.
6.8: Listen up, Jerusalem. Learn your lesson before I walk out on you. Don't make me turn this place into a ghost town."
6.9: The Lord said, "They gon' pick through what's left of Israel like harvesters lookin' for the last grapes—don't leave nothin'."
6.10: Who can I even talk to? Ain't nobody tryin' to hear Me. Their ears blocked, heart cold. My word's like trash to them—they don't want it.
6.11: I'm filled up with God's anger. I can't hold it in no more. Gotta pour it out on the kids, the grown folks, husbands and wives, old heads and young bucks—nobody safe.
6.12: Their houses, fields, and wives—gone. I'm stretchin' My hand against everybody in the land," says the Lord.
6.13: "From the broke to the bougie, they all greedy. Even the prophets and priests stay lyin'.
6.14: They act like they fixed the people's pain, sayin', 'It's all good, peace, peace!' But it ain't no peace!
6.15: Did they even feel bad when they did wrong? Nope. Couldn't even blush. That's why they gon' fall when judgment comes. I'm takin' 'em down," says the Lord.
6.16: The Lord said, "Stand at the crossroads, look around. Ask for the old paths, the good ones. Walk that road—you'll find rest for your soul." But they said, "We ain't walkin' that way."
6.17: I posted watchmen to warn y'all. Told you to listen for the trumpet. But they said, "Nah, we good."
6.18: So now the nations gon' hear this. Everybody, take notes—see what's goin' down.
6.19: Earth, listen up: I'm bringin' disaster on this crew, the consequences of their own thoughts. They ain't tryna hear My words, they threw out My law.
6.20: What good is incense from Sheba or imported sugar cane when your sacrifices don't mean nothin' to Me?
6.21: So yeah, I'm throwin' obstacles in front of 'em. Daddies and sons gon' trip. Neighbors, homies—everybody gon' fall."
6.22: The Lord says, "Here come the soldiers out the north—whole army risin' from way out.
6.23: They strapped with bows and spears. No mercy in 'em. They loud like a stormy sea, ridin' in deep on horses, ready for war against Zion's daughter."
6.24: We heard the news. Hands shakin'. Hearts racin'. Pain hittin' like labor contractions.
6.25: Don't even go outside. Don't walk nowhere. The enemy got swords everywhere. Fear's on every corner.
6.26: My people, mourn like you lost your only child. Put on that sackcloth. Roll in the ashes. The destroyer comin'—and it's gon' hit hard and fast.
6.27: God said, "I put you here to test these folks, to see what they really about."
6.28: But they hardheaded rebels. Always talkin' slick. Like dirty metal—bronze and iron—all of 'em corrupt.
6.29: The furnace burns hot. The lead's melted. But even with all that refining, the evil ones still won't come out right.
6.30: Folks gon' start callin' them 'rejected silver'—'cause the Lord ain't claimin' 'em no more.

7.1: This the word God gave Jeremiah:
7.2: "Stand at the church doors—right at the gate of the Lord's house— And shout this to everybody walkin' in to worship: 'Hear what the Lord say, y'all from Judah comin' up in here!'"
7.3: "The Lord of Heaven's Armies, Israel's God, says this: 'Fix how y'all livin' and how y'all treat people— And I'll let you stay in this land.'"
7.4: "Stop fallin' for them churchy lies like, 'The temple of the Lord! The temple of the Lord!' Just 'cause you here don't mean you safe."
7.5: "If you really switch up— Do right by folks, Handle justice between each other,
7.6: Stop oppressin' foreigners, orphans, and widows, Quit killin' the innocent, And stop chasin' after fake gods that do you dirty—
7.7: Then yeah, I'll let you stay in this land I gave your ancestors forever."
7.8: "But nah… Y'all trustin' in lies that won't help you."
7.9: "You stealin', killin', creepin' around, Swearin' false oaths, burnin' incense to Baal, And runnin' after gods you don't even know—"
7.10: "Then got the nerve to show up in My house talkin' about, 'We safe! We free!' So you can keep wildin'?"
7.11: "This house with My name on it? Y'all treatin' it like a hideout for thieves. But I see everything," says the Lord.
7.12: "Go look at Shiloh— That's where I used to put My name first. See what I did to it 'Cause of how Israel acted."
7.13: "Same thing happenin' now. I warned y'all over and over— But y'all ain't listen. I called, and y'all hit 'Ignore.'"
7.14: "So I'ma treat this temple— The one you put all your hope in— Just like Shiloh. I'ma shut it down."
7.15: "And I'ma throw you outta My sight Just like I did your cousins from Ephraim."
7.16: "Don't even pray for these people, Jeremiah. Don't cry, don't beg. I ain't listenin'."
7.17: "You see what they doin'? Out in the streets of Judah and Jerusalem?"
7.18: "Kids gather wood, Daddies start the fire, Mamas bakin' cakes for the 'queen of heaven.' They pourin' out drinks for fake gods— Tryna get a rise outta Me."
7.19: "But really, they just hurtin' theyself. They bringin' shame to they own face."
7.20: "So now My wrath is spillin' out On people, animals, trees, even the crops. It's gon' burn hot— Ain't nobody puttin' it out."
7.21: "Y'all might as well throw your burnt offerings On top of your regular food— Eat all of it. It don't mean nothin' to Me."
7.22: "When I brought your people outta Egypt, I ain't ask for burnt offerings— I said obey Me."
7.23: "I told them: 'Listen to My voice. I'll be your God. You'll be My people. Walk in My ways, and life'll go well.'"
7.24: "But they ain't listen. They followed they own shady hearts, Walked backwards instead of forward."
7.25: "Since day one, I been sendin' My prophets— Early, consistent, every single day."
7.26: "But they ain't hear Me. They stiffened up, Actin' worse than the folks before them."
7.27: "So yeah, go ahead and speak these words— But they not gon' listen. Call 'em—they not pickin' up."
7.28: "Say this: 'This nation don't listen to God. They don't accept correction. Truth packed up and left they mouth.'"
7.29: "Shave your head in mourning, Toss it away, Cry on the hills— The Lord done walked away from this generation."
7.30: "Judah's kids done evil right in My face," says the Lord. "They brought trash into My house And defiled it."
7.31: "They built altars at Tophet In the Valley of Hinnom— Burnin' their own kids alive. I never told them to do that. Never even crossed My mind."
7.32: "So now—soon—it won't be called Tophet no more, Or the Valley of Hinnom… It'll be known as the Valley of Slaughter."
7.33: "Dead bodies gon' be food for vultures and wild animals— And nobody gon' be around to chase them off."
7.34: "I'm shuttin' down all joy— Ain't gon' be no weddings, No parties, No laughter in Judah or Jerusalem. Just silence. Desolation."

8.1: "Around that time," says the Lord, "They gon' dig up the bones— Kings, princes, priests, prophets, regular folks— Everybody who lived in Jerusalem."
8.2: "And they gon' lay them bones out Under the sun, the moon, and the stars— All them things they used to love, serve, follow, chase, and worship. Ain't nobody gon' gather 'em up or bury 'em. They gon' be left out like trash."
8.3: "And the folks that's left— They gon' wish they was dead. 'Cause the pain gon' be so deep, They'd rather die than live," says the Lord of Heaven's Armies.
8.4: "Jeremiah, tell the people: 'If somebody fall, don't they get back up? If they turn off the road, don't they find their way back?'"
8.5: "But this crew? They stay fallin'. Jerusalem stuck in reverse— Holdin' on to lies, Refusin' to come back to Me."
8.6: "I been listenin'— Ain't nobody sayin' the right stuff. Ain't nobody askin', 'Dang... what have I done?' Everybody movin' fast— Like horses rushin' headfirst into battle."
8.7: "Even birds—storks, doves, swallows— They know when to migrate. But My people? They don't even know when judgment is knockin'."
8.8: "Y'all out here sayin', 'We wise. We got God's law.' But your scribes be writin' lies in the margins. They out here twistin' the truth."
8.9: "The so-called wise lookin' real dumb now. They ashamed, confused, caught slippin'. They rejected God's word— So how they gon' claim wisdom?"
8.10: "I'ma give they wives to strangers, And they land to somebody else. Everybody, high and low, Got greedy and dirty. Prophets and priests? All crooked."
8.11: "They out here puttin' a Band-Aid on bullet wounds, Sayin', 'Peace, peace,' When ain't no peace."
8.12: "And the worst part? They ain't even embarrassed. No shame. No blush. So when I bring judgment, They gon' fall like everybody else," says the Lord.
8.13: "I'm cleanin' house," says the Lord. "No grapes on the vine, No figs on the tree, Even the leaves gon' wither. Everything I gave 'em? Gone."
8.14: "Why we just sittin' around? Let's go hide in the strong cities. Let's be quiet and accept it— The Lord already shut us down. He gave us bitter water 'cause we sinned."
8.15: "We was lookin' for peace... But trouble pulled up instead. We hoped for healing— But it was all bad."
8.16: "We hear the enemy horses all the way from Dan. The whole land shook from their neighing. They came through and ate up the land, The cities, the people—everything."
8.17: "I'm sendin' snakes among y'all," says the Lord. "Vipers you can't charm. They gon' strike—and keep striking."
8.18: I tried to comfort myself... But I'm tired. Heart heavy.
8.19: Listen... That cry way off in the distance— That's My people. They say, "Isn't the Lord still in Zion? Ain't He still our King?" God answers: "Then why y'all keep makin' Me mad With these carved idols and knockoff gods?"
8.20: "The harvest passed. Summer's done. And we still not saved."
8.21: I'm tore up over what's happenin' to My people. Hurt deep. Grievin'. Straight up shocked.
8.22: "Ain't there no balm in Gilead? No doctors there? So why ain't My people healin'? Why they still out here broken?"

9.1: Man… if my head was full of water And my eyes flowed like a fountain, I'd be cryin' day and night For all the lives lost in My people's mess.
9.2: I wish I had a little cabin in the wilderness, Somewhere far from everybody— So I could leave these folks behind. They all cheatin', Snakes in the grass.
9.3: "They tongues like weapons— Lyin' is their favorite sport. Ain't no truth in the streets. They go from one foul act to the next, Actin' like they don't even know Me," says the Lord.
9.4: "Don't trust nobody. Your brother'll snake you, Your neighbor stay gossipin'."
9.5: "Everybody out here lyin' to each other. They trained they mouths to lie, Put in work just to do wrong."
9.6: "Your whole neighborhood built on lies. And with all this deceit, They still won't recognize Me," says the Lord.
9.7: So the Lord of Heaven's Armies says: "I'ma test 'em, Refine 'em like metal. 'Cause how else I'm supposed to deal with this?"
9.8: "They mouth speak peace, But they really plottin'. Their words sharp—like arrows."
9.9: "You think I ain't gon' handle this?" says the Lord. "You think I'm lettin' this slide?"
9.10: I'ma cry loud for the mountains, Mourn for the fields and forests. Ain't nobody left— Even the animals and birds done dipped.
9.11: "I'ma make Jerusalem a pile of rubble, A jackal's hangout. Judah's cities? Empty. No people."
9.12: Who wise enough to understand why? Why the land look scorched like this?
9.13: God says: "'Cause they walked away from My law. They ain't listen. They did whatever they felt like, Chasin' after fake gods they daddy's introduced."
9.14: "So I'ma give 'em bitter food, Nasty water to drink."
9.15: "I'ma scatter 'em all over the place— Among people they ain't never met. And I'ma send a sword behind 'em Till they done."
9.16: The Lord says: "Go call the mourning women. Get the ones who know how to cry right."
9.17: "Tell them: hurry up. Come cry for us. Let tears flood our faces."
9.18: The voice of sorrow ringin' from Zion: 'We been robbed! We ashamed! Kicked out our homes, Torn from the land!'"
9.19: "Listen, women: Hear God's word. Teach your daughters how to cry, Show your homegirls how to mourn."
9.20: "Death slid in through the window, Steppin' right into the palace. It took the kids—ain't no more playin' outside. Snatched the young men right off the block."
9.21: God says: "Bodies gon' be everywhere— Layin' out in the fields Like leftovers from harvest. Ain't nobody even pickin' 'em up."
9.22: This what the Lord say: "Don't brag on your smarts. Don't flex your muscles. Don't show off your riches."
9.23: "If you gon' brag, brag on this: That you know Me. That you understand I'm the Lord— Full of love, justice, and righteousness. That's the kind of stuff I vibe with," says the Lord.
9.24: "The days comin'," says the Lord, "Where I'ma deal with everybody— Circumcised or not. Egypt, Judah, Edom, Ammon, Moab— Even the folks out in the cut, Way out in the wilderness."
9.25: "All of 'em uncircumcised. And Israel? Yeah, y'all might be cut in the body— But y'all hearts still wild and unclean."
9.26: Egypt, Judah, Edom, Ammon, Moab—even them folks way out in the cut, livin' in the wild—all of 'em uncircumcised. But don't get it twisted, Israel too. Y'all got the mark on your body but not in your heart. Y'all hearts ain't been changed. God ain't impressed with outside religion when the inside still dirty.

10.1: Listen up, Israel— This the word the Lord speakin' straight to y'all:
10.2: "Don't follow the ways of them other nations. Don't be spooked by stars or signs in the sky— That's what got the Gentiles shook."
10.3: "All they customs? Straight up nonsense. They cut trees out the forest, Craft 'em with axes like it's art."
10.4: "Then they dress it up in silver and gold, Nail it down so it don't fall over. It's givin' pretty… but powerless."
10.5: "They stand tall like palm trees, But can't say a word. You gotta carry them 'cause they can't move theyself. Don't fear 'em— They can't hurt you. And they sure can't help you neither."
10.6: Ain't nobody like You, Lord. You mighty. Your name carry weight.
10.7: Who wouldn't respect You, King of the nations? That's what You deserve. Outta all the so-called wise folks and kingdoms— Ain't none compare to You.
10.8: These other nations? A bunch of fools— Fallin' for wooden statues And empty teachings.
10.9: They rockin' silver from Tarshish, Gold from Uphaz, All crafted by folks with tools. They got blue and purple robes on— But it's all just dress-up. Work of human hands.
10.10: But the Lord? He the real One. The living God. The forever King. When He gets angry, The whole earth trembles. Ain't no nation standin' up under that heat.
10.11: Tell 'em: "Any so-called god that ain't make heaven and earth? They gettin' wiped out— Gone from under the skies."
10.12: God made the earth with raw power. Set the world in place with wisdom. Stretched out the skies like a boss.
10.13: When He speaks, rainclouds show up. Water piles up in the sky. He makes lightning flash, And sends the wind out from His stash."
10.14: Everybody out here clueless— Craftsmen embarrassed by their fake gods. Them statues? Lies. Ain't no breath in 'em.
10.15: Worthless. Mistakes. And when judgment comes? They gon' be gone.
10.16: But Jacob's portion? He ain't like them. He made everything. And Israel is His. His name? The Lord of Heaven's Armies.
10.17: Pack your stuff, y'all livin' behind the walls— Time to go.
10.18: The Lord says: "I'm 'bout to toss the people out the land. I'ma shake things up So they feel what I'm sayin'."
10.19: "I'm hurt bad," says the people. "This pain deep… But I'ma carry it."
10.20: "My home got wrecked. My kids gone. Ain't nobody left to help set up the tent again."
10.21: "The leaders? Clueless. They ain't even checkin' for the Lord. So yeah—they failing, And all the people under 'em gettin' scattered."
10.22: You hear that rumblin'? News comin' from the north— Judah's cities 'bout to be left empty. Just jackals and silence.
10.23: Lord, I know this much: Humans don't run the show. We ain't built to guide ourselves right.
10.24: So correct me, Lord— But do it with care and justice. Not in full wrath— Or I'm done for.
10.25: Unleash that fury on the ones who don't know You, The ones who don't call on Your name. They ate up Jacob, Devoured us, Left our home in ruins.

11.1: This the word God gave to Jeremiah:
11.2: "Tell Judah and everybody in Jerusalem: Listen up—this covenant matter."
11.3: "This what the Lord God of Israel say: 'Cursed is anybody who don't follow the terms of this agreement—'"
11.4: "'The same one I gave y'all ancestors Back when I brought 'em outta Egypt, out that iron furnace. I said: Obey Me. Do what I say. Be My people, and I'll be your God.'"
11.5: "'That's how I'd keep My promise— To give y'all a land flowin' with milk and honey, Just like I told your forefathers.'" And I said, "Amen, Lord. Say less."
11.6: Then the Lord told me, "Preach this all through Judah, Out loud in the streets of Jerusalem: 'Y'all need to actually do what the covenant says.'"
11.7: "'From day one—when I brought y'all outta Egypt— I been tellin' y'all, day in and day out: Obey Me!'"
11.8: "'But nah… they ain't wanna hear it. Everybody kept followin' they own wicked ways. So now they gotta deal with the consequences Of a covenant they never took seriously.'"
11.9: Then the Lord said, "There's a whole conspiracy brewin' in Judah and Jerusalem."
11.10: "They slid back into the same foolishness Their ancestors was on— Ignoring Me. Chasin' after other gods. Both Israel and Judah done broke the deal I made with their people."
11.11: "So here's what I'm bringin': Trouble they can't run from. And when they finally call on Me? I ain't pickin' up."
11.12: "They gon' run to them fake gods they been burnin' incense to— But guess what? Them gods ain't savin' nobody when the heat hits."
11.13: "Y'all got as many fake gods as you got cities. Altars to Baal on every block in Jerusalem."
11.14: "So Jeremiah, don't even pray for 'em. Don't cry. Don't plead. I'm not listenin' when they finally start beggin'."
11.15: "Why My people tryna pull up to My house Actin' holy, when they out here wildin'? They celebratin' evil like it's cute. That 'holy flesh' they brought? It don't mean nothin' now."
11.16: "I used to call you My green olive tree— Healthy, beautiful, full of good fruit. But now I'ma set fire to it. The branches gettin' chopped off."
11.17: "The same Lord who planted you Just pronounced judgment— 'Cause both Israel and Judah got Me heated Burnin' incense to Baal and bringin' destruction on theyselves."
11.18: Then the Lord let me in on somethin'. I saw what was goin' down— 'Cause He showed me the whole plot.
11.19: I was movin' like a lamb headin' to slaughter— Didn't even know folks was plottin' on me. They was sayin': "Cut him down like a tree. End his life. Erase his name from the earth."
11.20: But You, Lord of Heaven's Armies, You judge fair. You see hearts and motives. So I'm askin'—let me see You handle 'em. I'm bringin' this case to You.
11.21: And this what the Lord said about them folks in Anathoth That was tryin' to kill me— Talkin' 'bout, "Stop prophesyin' in the Lord's name Or we gon' take you out."
11.22: The Lord said: "Bet. I got somethin' for 'em. The young men? Killed by the sword. Their kids? Gon' starve."
11.23: "Ain't gon' be no leftovers. I'ma bring judgment down heavy On the whole city of Anathoth. Their time is up."

12.1: Lord, You always right when I bring my case to You— But I gotta ask somethin' real… Why the wicked out here winnin'? Why fake folks stay smilin' and comfy?
12.2: You the One who let 'em grow— They got roots now. They out here bearin' fruit. Talkin' like they close to You, But they don't think about You at all.
12.3: But You know me, Lord. You done seen my heart. You tested me. So go head—snatch 'em out like sheep for slaughter. Line 'em up for what's comin'.
12.4: How long the land gotta grieve? Why all the plants dryin' up? The animals and birds gone too— All 'cause these people out here wildin'. They really think You not gon' catch up to 'em?
12.5: God replied: "If you tired runnin' with folks on foot, How you gon' keep up when horses start runnin'? If you stressed in a calm land, What you gon' do when the flood hits near the Jordan?"
12.6: "Even your own family got smoke for you. They smilin' in your face, But don't trust 'em— They callin' folks to come for you behind your back."
12.7: "I had to let go of My house. I stepped away from My people. The one I loved? I handed her over to her enemies."
12.8: "She supposed to be Mine, But now she roarin' at Me like a wild lion. So yeah… I can't even claim her no more."
12.9: "My people turned into some spotted vulture, Gettin' circled by other birds. Go ahead—bring all the wild animals. Let 'em feast."
12.10: "So many rulers stomped through My vineyard, Treated it like trash. They wrecked My garden, Turned it into wilderness."
12.11: "Now the land cryin' out to Me. Everything desolate. And ain't nobody even care."
12.12: "Raiders showin' up on every hilltop. And the sword of the Lord Gon' sweep from one side of the land to the other. Ain't nobody gon' know peace."
12.13: "They plantin' wheat but harvestin' thorns. All that grindin'—no payoff. Shame gon' cover they harvest, 'Cause My wrath ain't lettin' up."
12.14: The Lord says: "All them shady neighbors who try touch what I gave My people? I'ma yank 'em out they own land— And I'ma pull Judah up outta their mix too."
12.15: "But after I pluck 'em out, I'ma show 'em some grace. Bring 'em back to their own spot, Each one to their own hood."
12.16: "And if they learn how My people move— If they say 'As the Lord lives' like they used to say 'Baal lives,' I'll let 'em live among My people."
12.17: "But if they don't listen? I'ma tear that nation up from the roots. Gone. For good," says the Lord.

13.1: The Lord told me, "Go grab you a linen belt. Wrap it around your waist— But don't let it touch no water."
13.2: So I did what He said, Got the belt and wore it.
13.4: "Take that belt you rockin', Head over to the Euphrates River, And hide it in a crack in the rocks."
13.5: So I packed up and hid it there—just like He told me.
13.6: After a while, God said, "Now go back to the Euphrates And dig up that belt I told you to stash."
13.7: I did, and sure enough— The belt was ruined. Tore up. Worthless.
13.8: Then God hit me with this:
13.9: "This how I'ma ruin the pride of Judah— And the pride Jerusalem swear they got."
13.10: "These people hardheaded. They won't listen. They out here followin' whatever their hearts say, Worshippin' fake gods. So now they just like that belt— Useless."
13.11: "I wanted 'em to stay close to Me— Like a belt clings to your waist. They was supposed to be My people, My name, My glory out loud. But they ain't wanna hear Me."
13.12: God said, "Tell 'em this: 'Every bottle gon' get filled with wine.'" And they gon' say, "Duh. Of course every bottle get filled with wine."
13.13: But hit 'em back with this: "The Lord says: I'm fillin' all y'all—kings, priests, prophets, regular folks— With drunken confusion."
13.14: "Y'all gon' crash into each other— Fathers and sons both. No mercy. No pity. No holdin' back. I'ma wreck y'all."
13.15: Listen up! Don't let your pride talk over God. He already said what He said.
13.16: Give God His glory before things go dark. Before your feet trip up in the night, And what you thought was light Turns into death's shadow.
13.17: But if you still ain't listenin'? Then I'ma cry behind closed doors for y'all. Big tears. Heavy sorrow. 'Cause the Lord's people gettin' snatched up.
13.18: Tell the king and his mama: "Y'all better sit down and humble yourselves. That crown? It comin' off."
13.19: The southern cities? Locked up tight. Ain't nobody openin' nothin'. Judah's gettin' taken, Every last one of 'em.
13.20: Look up north— See who comin' for you. Where the people you was supposed to protect at? Your fine flock?
13.21: What you gon' say When God flip the script on you? You trained them enemies to lead you— Now they doin' just that.
13.22: If you sittin' there wonderin', "Why this happenin' to me?" It's 'cause your sin too loud. God exposin' you—skirt lifted, feet bare.
13.23: Can a Black person switch they skin? Can a leopard drop its spots? Then what makes you think You can do right when all you know is wrong?
13.24: That's why I'ma blow y'all away like desert dust.
13.25: This your portion from Me, 'Cause you forgot Me And put your trust in lies.
13.26: I'ma pull your skirt over your face So everybody see your shame.
13.27: I seen what you been up to— The cheating, the lust, The wild behavior on every hill. It's nasty. Woe to you, Jerusalem. What's it gon' take For you to get right?

14.1: This the word God gave Jeremiah about the drought.
14.2: Judah cryin'. The city gates saggin'. Folks mournin' for the land— Jerusalem's cries echoin' through the air.
14.3: The rich sent they servants to fetch water. They got to the wells—bone dry. Came back with empty jars, Head hangin', faces full of shame.
14.4: The ground was cracked and dry— Ain't no rain fell in a minute. Even the farmers was embarrassed, Pullin' they cloaks over they heads.
14.5: Out in the fields, even the deer gave birth, Then dipped—'cause no grass was growin'.
14.6: Wild donkeys stood on the hills, Sniffin' the air like stray dogs. Eyes dim from hunger. Ain't no grass nowhere.
14.7: Lord, we know our sins speak loud… But for Your name's sake—please move! Yeah, we messed up a lot, But we still Yours.
14.8: You the Hope of Israel— Our help when trouble hit. Why You movin' like You don't even stay here? Like You just passin' through?
14.9: Why You lookin' shocked, like You can't save? But Lord, You with us. We reppin' Your name. Don't leave us hangin'.
14.10: But God said: "They stay wanderin' off—feet just doin whatever. I ain't acceptin' that. I'm done overlookin'. They 'bout to feel this judgment."
14.11: Then the Lord told me, "Don't pray for them no more. Not for they good."
14.12: "When they fast—I ain't listenin'. When they bring offerings—I ain't acceptin' that. What's comin'? Sword. Famine. Disease."
14.13: Then I said, "But Lord, The prophets out here tellin' folks, 'Ain't gon' be no sword. Ain't gon' be no famine. Peace comin' for sure.'"
14.14: God clapped back: "They lyin' on My name. I ain't send 'em. Ain't tell 'em nothin'. They makin' up visions, Fake prophecies, lies from they own hearts."
14.15: "So here's what's gon' happen to them prophets talkin' 'No sword, no famine': They gon' die by sword and famine. Period."
14.16: "And the folks that listened? Left out in the streets. No funerals. No burials. Wives, sons, daughters—all of 'em. Their sins caught up to 'em."
14.17: God told me, "Say this to the people: 'My tears fall nonstop, day and night. My people been hit hard— Like a young daughter with a fatal blow.'"
14.18: "I walk outside—bodies in the field. I step in the city—folks dyin' from hunger. Prophets and priests wanderin' lost, Don't even recognize the land no more."
14.19: Lord… have You really given up on Judah? You done with Zion? Why You hit us like this and ain't no healing? We hoped for peace… But pain came instead.
14.20: We own up to it, Lord— Our sins. Our parents' sins. We wrong. We admit it.
14.21: Don't reject us, Lord—do it for Your name. Don't throw Your throne in the dirt. Remember Your covenant. Don't break it.
14.22: Can idols make it rain? Can the skies rain on command? Nah—it's only You, Lord. That's why we waitin' on You… You the one who controls it all.

15.1: Then the Lord told me straight up: "Even if Moses and Samuel was standin' here beggin', I still wouldn't change My mind about this crew. Tell 'em: 'Y'all gotta go.' Get out My face."
15.2: And if they ask, "Where we supposed to go?" Say this: "The Lord said: Some gon' die—so they gon' die. Some gon' get sliced up—so the sword for them. Some gon' starve—famine waitin'. Some gettin' locked up—captivity for them."
15.3: "I'm sendin' four ways to break 'em," says the Lord: "Swords to kill, Dogs to drag, Birds to peck, Beasts to feast."
15.4: "I'ma let 'em be embarrassed all across the nations. And it's all 'cause of what Manasseh—Hezekiah's son—did in Jerusalem."
15.5: "Ain't nobody gon' care about you, Jerusalem. Nobody feelin' bad. Ain't even gon' ask how you doin'."
15.6: "You left Me. You turned back. So now I'ma stretch out My hand and tear it all down. I'm tired of holdin' back."
15.7: "I'ma scatter y'all like wheat in the wind— Right at the city gates. I'ma take y'all children. I'ma wreck what's Mine, Since y'all don't wanna come back."
15.8: "Too many widows to count—like sand by the sea. Mamas losin' sons in broad daylight. Pain gon' drop outta nowhere—fear too."
15.9: "That woman who had seven sons? She gon' be crushed. Her light gon' go out in the middle of the day. She gon' be ashamed. What's left of her boys? I'm handin' them over to the sword."
15.10: Jeremiah said: "Man, why I even born, Mama? I stay beefin' with everybody. I ain't owe nobody money. Ain't nobody owe me. But folks curse me anyway."
15.11: The Lord replied: "Don't worry—I got a remnant gon' ride with you. Even your enemies gon' come beggin' for you When the pressure hit."
15.12: "Can anybody break iron from the north? Iron that's mixed with bronze? Nah."
15.13: "I'm givin' your riches and treasures away— No price tag, no mercy. All 'cause y'all been sinnin' everywhere you go."
15.14: "I'ma make you cross into a foreign land with your enemies. I lit a fire in My anger— And it ain't goin' out."
15.15: Jeremiah said: "Lord, You know me. Don't forget about me. Please come see about me. Get back at the folks who tryna take me out. You know I took this heat for You."
15.16: "I found Your word—ate it up. It gave me joy. It filled my heart. You put Your name on me, Lord of Heaven's Armies."
15.17: "I ain't sit with clowns or jokers. Didn't laugh, didn't join the foolishness. I stayed solo 'cause Your hand was heavy on me. You put fire in my bones."
15.18: "But why this pain still hangin' on? Why this wound won't heal? Lord, are You gon' be like a stream that dries up on me? A river that ghosted me?"
15.19: Then the Lord said: "If you come back right, I'll bring you back in. You'll stand before Me again. If you learn to separate what's good from all that mess, You'll speak for Me again."
15.20: "I'ma make you like a bronze wall to these folks. They gon' try you— But they can't beat you. 'Cause I'm with you to save and rescue you," says the Lord.
15.21: "I'ma pull you outta wicked hands. I'ma snatch you from the grip of the ruthless."

16.1: God came to me with another word.
16.2: He said, "Don't get married, Jeremiah. Don't have no kids in this place."
16.3: "Why? 'Cause them kids born here, And their mamas and daddies too— They all gon' die messed up deaths."
16.4: "Ain't nobody gon' cry for 'em or bury 'em. They gon' be laid out in the street like trash. Birds and wild animals gon' eat their bodies. Famine and war takin' 'em out."
16.5: "And don't go to no funerals. Don't mourn or show sympathy. I took My peace away from these folks," says the Lord. "No more love. No more mercy."
16.6: "From the big shots to the nobodies, They all gon' die. No burials, no eulogies. Ain't nobody cuttin' theyself or shavin' they head in grief."
16.7: "No one breakin' bread for mournin', No 'I'm sorry for your loss' meals, No comfort drinks for nobody's mama or daddy."
16.8: "Don't even pull up at no parties, either. Don't eat. Don't toast with 'em."
16.9: "I'ma make the joy stop," says the Lord. "No more laughs, No more weddings, No more turn-ups. You gon' see it happen with your own eyes."
16.10: "When you tell them all this, They gon' ask: 'Why God trippin' like this? What we even do?'"
16.11: "Tell 'em: 'Y'all daddies left Me for fake gods— Served 'em, bowed to 'em, forgot all about Me. Didn't keep My Word.'"
16.12: "But y'all? Y'all worse than they was. Everybody doin' whatever their wicked heart tell 'em. Ain't nobody listenin' to Me."
16.13: "So now I'ma throw y'all out this land— Into some foreign place y'all never known. And over there, you gon' serve them fake gods 24/7. And I ain't showin' no favor."
16.14: "But one day soon," says the Lord, "People ain't gon' say, 'God brought Israel outta Egypt' no more."
16.15: "They gon' say, 'God brought Israel outta the North— Outta all the places He scattered them.' And I'ma bring y'all back home To the land I gave your ancestors."
16.16: "I'm sendin' out fishers first— They gon' hook y'all one by one. Then I'ma send hunters— They gon' track y'all down from every cave, hill, and hole."
16.17: "Ain't nothin' you do hidden from Me. I see all your mess. And yeah, I'm watchin'."
16.18: "First, I'ma pay y'all double for the dirt y'all done. Y'all polluted My land with y'all idol worship And all them disgusting sacrifices."
16.19: Then I said: "Lord, You my strength, my safe spot, my cover when it's hard. Nations gon' come from all over sayin': 'Our ancestors lied to us— Gave us nothin' but fake gods and nonsense.'"
16.20: "Can folks even make real gods for theyself? Nah—those ain't even gods!"
16.21: "So I'ma show 'em— For real this time— Who I am and how I move. They gon' know My name is the Lord."

17.1: Judah's sin? Man, it's carved in deep— Like somebody scratched it in stone with a diamond tip. It's written on they hearts and even on the altars they worship at.
17.2: Even they kids remember the wild worship parties With them fake gods under the trees on the hills.
17.3: "I'ma take everything from y'all— Your riches, your treasures, Even the so-called 'sacred' spots you turned sinful."
17.4: "You gon' lose the land I gave you. You gon' serve your enemies In a land you don't even know. You lit a fire in Me, And that anger ain't goin' nowhere."
17.5: The Lord says: "Cursed is the one who puts all their trust in other people, Who lean on human strength, And forget 'bout Me."
17.6: "They gon' be like dry bushes in the desert— Ain't gon' see no blessings, Just stuck in a salty, lonely place Where life don't grow."
17.7: "But the one who trusts Me? They blessed for real."
17.8: "They like a tree right by the river— Roots deep, leaves green, No stress when the heat hit, Still bearin' fruit in drought season."
17.9: "The heart?" It's shady. Trickier than anything out here. It's sick. Who really understands it?"
17.10: "But I do," says the Lord. "I check hearts. I test minds. And I pay folks back Based on what they really out here doin'."
17.11: "Gettin' rich the wrong way? That's like sittin' on eggs that never hatch. All that fake flexin' gon' fade, And you gon' look like a fool in the end."
17.12: God's throne been sittin' high since day one— That's our true place of worship.
17.13: Lord, You the only hope Israel got. Whoever walks away from You? Shame gon' follow. They names gon' be dust 'Cause they turned from the fountain of living water.
17.14: "Heal me, Lord—and I'll be healed. Save me—and I'll be saved. You the only one I praise."
17.15: Folks keep jokin': "Where that word from God at? Let's see it then."
17.16: "But Lord, You know I stayed faithful. I ain't run from my calling, I ain't ask for doom— I just said what You gave me."
17.17: "Please don't be scary to me, God. You my only safety net when the world's fallin' apart."
17.18: "Let them haters fall, not me. Let them be shook, Not me. Let Your judgment hit them hard— Double it if You got to!"
17.19: Then the Lord told me, "Go stand at the main gate where the kings roll in and out, And tell everybody this word—Judah, Jerusalem, all of 'em."
17.21: "God say: 'Don't carry no load or do no work on the Sabbath. Don't bring your hustle through these gates on that day.'"
17.22: "Keep the Sabbath holy, Just like I told your ancestors."
17.23: "But they ain't listen. They got hard-headed, Blocked their ears, Wouldn't take no correction."
17.24: "If y'all take Me serious And stop the work on Sabbath, Respectin' it like you supposed to—"
17.25: "Then kings gon' keep ridin' through these gates, Sittin' on David's throne, Bringing praises, And this city? It'll stand forever."
17.26: "Folks from all over—Judah, Jerusalem, Benjamin, the hills and valleys— Gon' bring offerings and worship Me right."
17.27: "But if y'all keep treatin' the Sabbath like it don't matter— Still carryin' loads and breakin' rules— Then I'ma set these gates on fire. Jerusalem's palaces gon' burn, And nobody gon' put that fire out."

18.1: This what the Lord told Jeremiah:
18.2: "Get up, go down to the potter's shop. I got somethin' to show you."
18.3: So I pulled up to the spot— Dude was workin' the wheel, shapin' clay.
18.4: The jar he was makin' got messed up in his hands, So he reshaped it into somethin' else, Whatever he thought looked right.
18.6: "Y'all see this? Israel, can't I do the same with y'all as this potter? You the clay—I'm the one holdin' you."
18.7: "If I say I'm 'bout to tear down a nation—
18.8: But they flip the script and turn from evil? Then cool—I'ma back off the punishment."
18.9: "Same way, if I say I'm 'bout to build somethin' up—
18.10: But they start actin' shady? Then nah, they ain't gettin' that blessing no more."
18.11: "So go tell the folks in Judah and Jerusalem: 'I'm plottin' judgment, and it's comin' fast. So switch up your ways. Start doin' right—right now.'"
18.12: But they said, "Ain't no point. We gon' do what we wanna do anyway. We gon' follow our hearts—even if they wicked."
18.13: So God clapped back: "Ask the nations— Who ever heard of somethin' this wild? Israel actin' like they ain't got no home training."
18.14: "Who leaves fresh snow water from Lebanon? Who trades in cold, clean streams For dirty, foreign runoff?"
18.15: "That's what My people did. They forgot Me. Started burnin' incense to trash idols. They left the real path And got lost in back alleys."
18.16: "Now they land gon' be empty and cursed— So bad folks gon' just shake they heads when they pass by."
18.17: "I'ma scatter them like dry leaves in the wind. When trouble hits, They gon' see My back, not My face."
18.18: Then the haters said, "Let's shut Jeremiah up. We still got priests, we still got wisdom, We still got other prophets. Let's come at him with slick talk And ignore whatever he sayin'."
18.19: I said, "Lord, You hear this, right? They tryna take me out."
18.20: "I was speakin' up for them— Beggin' You not to wild out. And this how they repay me? By diggin' a grave with my name on it?"
18.21: "So let the consequences fall, Lord. Let they kids go hungry, Let the soldiers hit 'em hard, Take they men, take they peace."
18.22: "Let the war cries hit they homes Like a surprise attack— 'Cause they straight up plotted on me."
18.23: "You see it, Lord. You know they schemes. Don't forgive 'em. Don't wipe it clean. Let judgment hit 'em hard— And don't hold back."

19.1: God told Jeremiah, "Go buy a clay jar from the potter, And take some OGs—elders from the people and the priests—with you."
19.2: "Take 'em to the Valley of Hinnom, Right by the Potsherd Gate, And speak what I'm 'bout to tell you."
19.3: "Say this to Judah's kings and folks in Jerusalem: 'Listen up! This what the Lord of Heaven's Armies say— I'm about to drop judgment so heavy, It'll make folks ears ring when they hear it.'"
19.4: "'Why? 'Cause y'all turned your back on Me. Made this land foreign—burnin' incense to fake gods Y'all don't even know. And worse, y'all spilled innocent blood out here.'"
19.5: "'Built altars to Baal, Burned y'all own kids in fire like it was an offering! I ain't never told y'all to do that mess. Didn't even cross My mind.'"
19.6: "'So now, days comin' where this place Ain't gon' be called Tophet or the Valley of Hinnom no more. It's gon' be called the Valley of Slaughter.'"
19.7: "'Right here, I'ma shut down all Judah's plans. They gon' fall by the sword, And the folks chasin' 'em down Gon' leave their bodies for the birds and wild animals.'"
19.8: "'This city gon' be so wrecked, People gon' walk by like "What happened here?" It'll be nothin' but ruins and sickness.'"
19.9: "'It'll get so bad, they gon' eat their own kids Just tryin' to survive the siege. Neighbors eatin' neighbors. That's how deep the desperation gon' go.'"
19.10: Then God said, "Jeremiah, break that flask Right in front of the elders."
19.11: "Tell 'em: 'This what God say— Just like this jar broke, That's how I'm gon' break this people and this city. Ain't no gluin' it back together. They gon' bury folks in Tophet Till there ain't no space left.'"
19.12: "'I'ma make this city just like Tophet. Disrespected. Desecrated. Destroyed.'"
19.13: "'Even the royal cribs gon' be filthy— 'Cause they out here burnin' incense on rooftops To the stars and pourin' out drinks to idols. Every last house stank of rebellion.'"
19.14: After all that, Jeremiah left Tophet And came back to the temple court. He faced the people and dropped the mic one more time:
19.15: "Y'all better listen—this from the Lord of Heaven's Armies: I'm bringin' every bit of that judgment I said I would 'Cause y'all got stiff necks And straight up refused to listen."

20.1: So Pashhur, son of Immer—one of the top priests and chief of security at the Lord's house— Heard what Jeremiah been sayin'.
20.2: Man got mad, hit Jeremiah, and had him thrown in stocks near the Benjamin Gate by the temple.
20.3: Next day, Pashhur let him out. But Jeremiah wasn't done—he said, "God ain't callin' you Pashhur no more. Your new name? Magor-Missabib—'Terror All Around.'"
20.4: "'Cause this what God say: I'ma make you a whole nightmare to yourself and all your friends. Y'all gon' watch each other fall by enemy swords. Babylon gon' take Judah, And they ain't gon' be gentle with it."
20.5: "The city's money, crops, jewels, treasures— All of it gettin' looted. Your enemies takin' it straight to Babylon."
20.6: "And you, Pashhur—you and your whole household? Y'all goin' too. Y'all gon' die over there, You and everybody you been lyin' to."
20.7: Jeremiah said, "Lord… You pulled me into this, And I said yes. Now I'm the joke of the day— They clown me nonstop."
20.8: "Every time I speak, it's judgment. Violence. Destruction. Your words made me a punchline."
20.9: "I tried to quit. I really did. I said, 'I'm done talkin' about God.' But yo… it was like FIRE Locked up in my bones. I got tired of holdin' it back. I couldn't keep quiet."
20.10: "Everybody sayin', 'Terror everywhere!' They tryna snitch—'Go ahead, report him!' Even folks I thought I knew Waitin' on me to slip, Schemin' for revenge."
20.11: "But the Lord with me like a warrior. My haters gon' trip and fall— They ain't gon' win. They gon' be embarrassed forever. Never gon' live it down."
20.12: "Lord of Heaven's Armies, You test hearts and motives— Let me see justice done. I laid my case at Your feet."
20.13: "Sing to the Lord! Praise Him! He came through for the broke and beat down, Snatched us outta evil hands."
20.14: Then Jeremiah spiraled again— "Cursed be the day I was born. Don't celebrate my birthday no more."
20.15: "Forget the man who told my pops, 'It's a boy!'— He shouldn't have been so happy."
20.16: "Let him end up like Sodom—no mercy. Let him wake up to screams, Hear chaos at lunch."
20.17: "Shoulda just died in the womb. Let my mama's belly be my coffin."
20.18: "Why was I even born? Just to suffer? Just to feel pain and shame all my days?"

21.1: This the word God gave Jeremiah when King Zedekiah sent Pashhur son of Melchiah and Zephaniah son of Maaseiah, the priest, to holla at him.
21.2: They said, "Can you talk to the Lord for us? Nebuchadnezzar out here wagin' war, and maybe—just maybe—God gon' do one of His miracles like before and make Babylon back off."
21.3: But Jeremiah replied, "Tell Zedekiah this right here—
21.4: 'This what the Lord, God of Israel, said: I'ma flip the script. The very weapons y'all holdin' to fight Babylon with? I'ma turn them against y'all. I'ma let them Babylonian soldiers walk right into the city.
21.5: And I ain't sittin' this one out—I'm fightin' you, not them. My hand stretched out, My arm strong, and I'm comin' with anger, fury, and smoke.
21.6: I'ma hit this whole city—people and animals alike. A deadly plague gon' sweep through.
21.7: And after that? Zedekiah, his crew, and whoever still alive from famine, sword, or disease—I'ma hand y'all over to Nebuchadnezzar. Y'all enemies gon' get y'all, and he ain't showin' no mercy. No pity. No chill.'"
21.8: "Now tell the people this," Jeremiah continued. "This what the Lord say: 'I'm givin' y'all two choices—life or death.
21.9: If you stay in this city, you gon' die—by sword, starvation, or sickness. But if you surrender to Babylon and go out to them, you'll live. Your life'll be the only thing you keep, but that's better than nothin'.
21.10: I done turned My face against this city, not for it. It's over. Babylon gon' take it and burn it down. Period.'"
21.11: And to the royal fam—yeah, the House of David—God got something to say:
21.12: "Wake up and do right, early in the morning! Rescue the ones gettin' robbed. If not, My anger gon' blaze up like a wildfire, And y'all won't be able to put it out. It's gon' burn 'cause of y'all's wickedness."
21.13: "I'm comin' for you too," says the Lord. "You sit up high in the valley, feelin' safe on your lil' hill, Actin' like, 'Who gon' check us? Who can step up in here?'
21.14: Well, I'ma check you. I'ma judge you by your actions, And I'ma light a fire in your woods, And everything around you? It's gettin' torched."

22.1: The Lord said, "Go down to the king's crib in Judah and give him this word.
22.2: Tell him, 'Listen up, king of Judah—you sittin' on David's throne. You, your servants, and everybody who come through these gates, hear what the Lord gotta say!
22.3: This what the Lord says: Do right. Judge fair. Save the folks being robbed. Don't mistreat or hurt the foreigners, the orphans, or the widows. And don't be out here spillin' innocent blood in this place.
22.4: If y'all really do this, then kings from David's line gon' ride through them gates again—on horses and in chariots—with they people and crews behind them.
22.5: But if y'all ignore what I'm sayin', I swear on Myself," says the Lord, "this whole palace gon' end up in ruins."
22.6: The Lord got this to say about the king's house: "You might be like Gilead to Me, Or like the heights of Lebanon, But I'ma still turn you into a wasteland, A bunch of ghost towns with no one in 'em.
22.7: I'ma bring wreckers with tools To chop down your best cedar wood And toss it in the fire."
22.8: When the nations walk by and see Jerusalem lookin' like a graveyard, they gon' ask, "What happened? Why'd the Lord do this to such a great city?"
22.9: And the answer gon' be, "'Cause they broke the Lord's covenant and ran off worshipin' fake gods."
22.10: Don't cry for the ones already dead. Cry for the ones who get exiled, 'Cause they ain't never comin' back home.
22.11: This what the Lord says about Shallum (a.k.a. Jehoahaz), son of Josiah, who ruled after him: He ain't comin' back here no more.
22.12: He gon' die in the foreign land where they dragged him, and he'll never see Judah again.
22.13: Woe to the one who builds his house off shady deals, Who don't pay folks what they earned, Just usin' people like they ain't human.
22.14: Talkin' 'bout, "I'mma build me a big house, real fly, Decked out with cedar and painted all nice."
22.15: You think bein' surrounded by cedar make you royalty? Your daddy—Josiah—he ate, drank, And he still did what was right. That's why it went well for him.
22.16: He looked out for the poor and the needy— That's what it really means to know Me," says the Lord.
22.17: But you? Your eyes only see greed. You shed innocent blood. You oppress. You abuse. You wildin'.
22.18: So the Lord says this about Jehoiakim, son of Josiah: Ain't nobody gon' mourn him. No "RIP my brother!" No "Alas, my king!"
22.19: He gon' get tossed out like a dead donkey, Dragged outside the city gates and left there.
22.20: Climb up to Lebanon and cry your heart out, Scream from Bashan, Cry from the peaks— 'Cause all your homies gone.
22.21: I tried talkin' to you when you had it good, But you ain't wanna hear it. That's been your vibe since way back—you never listened.
22.22: Now the wind gon' blow away your leaders, Your allies gon' get snatched up, And that's when the shame and regret gon' hit you hard.
22.23: You livin' all comfy in cedar palaces, But when the pain hit, You gon' squirm like a woman givin' birth.
22.24: The Lord said, "Even if Coniah (a.k.a. Jehoiachin), son of Jehoiakim, was a ring on My hand, I'd still snatch him off.
22.25: I'ma hand him over to the folks tryin' to kill him— Nebuchadnezzar and the Babylonians.
22.26: Him and his mama gon' get exiled to a place they ain't even from, And that's where they'll die.
22.27: They wish they could come back, But that wish ain't comin' true.
22.28: Coniah—he ain't nothin' but a broken, tossed-away piece of pottery. Him and his family—rejected and exiled to a strange land.
22.29: Earth, earth, earth—listen up! This what the Lord say:
22.30: 'Write this man down as childless. Ain't none of his descendants gon' sit on David's throne, Or run things in Judah ever again.'"

23.1: "Woe to the so-called leaders who out here wreckin' My people and tearin' up My flock," says the Lord.
23.2: So this what the Lord, the God of Israel, got to say to the ones supposed to be feedin' His people: "Y'all scattered My flock, pushed 'em away, and ain't even checked on 'em. Don't worry—I'ma check on y'all real close for all that mess you been doing."
23.3: "But I'ma gather up the rest of My people from all the spots I had to send 'em to, and bring them back home safe. They gon' grow and multiply again."
23.4: "I'ma raise up real leaders over them—ones that feed them right. They won't be scared, stressed, or missing anymore," says the Lord.
23.5: "The days coming," says the Lord, "When I'ma raise up from David's line A real one—righteous, just, and wise. A King that's gon' rule right and win.
23.6: When He reigns, Judah gon' be safe, Israel gon' live secure. And His name gon' be: THE LORD OUR RIGHTEOUSNESS."
23.7: "Look, the time's comin'," says the Lord, "where folks won't be sayin', 'As surely as the Lord brought Israel outta Egypt,'
23.8: but instead they gon' say, 'As surely as the Lord brought us back from the north and all over the world where He scattered us.' And they gon' live in their own land again."
23.9: My heart is shattered Because of these so-called prophets. I'm shakin' in my bones. I feel like I'm drunk or high, But really, it's from the weight of the Lord's words.
23.10: The land full of cheaters and backstabbers. The whole earth mournin'. Even the wild places lookin' dry. Why? 'Cause these folks wicked, and their strength ain't even real.
23.11: "Both the prophets and the priests outta pocket. I done caught 'em wildin' out— Even in My own house," says the Lord.
23.12: "So now they walkin' on slippery ground, Gon' fall in the dark. I'm bringin' disaster down on 'em— This they year to feel it," says the Lord.
23.13: "The prophets in Samaria was already trippin'— They was out here speakin' for Baal, Leadin' My people off track.
23.14: But them prophets in Jerusalem? Whew. They cheatin', lyin', helpin' evil folks stay evil. Ain't nobody repentin'. To Me, they lookin' like Sodom and Gomorrah out here."
23.15: "So here's what the Lord of Heaven's Armies say: I'ma serve these prophets some bitter wormwood tea, And have 'em drink poison water. They done infected the whole land with they foolishness."
23.16: This what the Lord says: "Stop listenin' to these fake prophets. They gassin' y'all up. They talkin' dreams they made up— Ain't nothin' come from Me."
23.17: They out here tellin' rebels, 'God said y'all gon' have peace.' And tellin' folks followin' they own ways, 'Ain't nothin' bad gon' happen to you.'
23.18: But who really stood in My inner circle? Who actually heard My words?
23.19: Watch out—God's storm is comin'. It's fierce. It's gon' slam the wicked upside the head.
23.20: The Lord ain't lettin' up Till He get done with what's in His heart. Later, y'all gon' finally get it.
23.21: "I ain't send these prophets, But they ran anyway. I ain't speak to 'em, But they prophesied anyway.
23.22: If they had sat down and listened to Me, They woulda turned folks away from their sin.
23.23: Y'all think I'm just a local God?" says the Lord. "You think I ain't everywhere?
23.24: You think folks can hide from Me? Don't I fill the whole universe?"
23.25: "I heard what them dream-havin', lie-tellin' prophets said: 'I had a dream from the Lord!'
23.26: How long they gon' keep lyin' like this? These dreams they dreamin'? They comin' from they own twisted hearts.
23.27: They tryna make My people forget Me, Just like their ancestors forgot Me for Baal.
23.28: If a prophet got a dream, fine—let him share it. But if he got My word, He better preach that truth straight up. Wheat ain't the same as chaff," says the Lord.
23.29: "Ain't My word like fire? Like a hammer that shatters rock?"
23.30: "I'm against these prophets," says the Lord, "Who out here copyin' each other's fake messages, Like they mine."
23.31: "I'm against the ones Who twist up words and blame it on Me, Like I said it."
23.32: "I'm against them dream-sellin' prophets Who lead My people astray with their lies. They reckless, I ain't send them, And they ain't helpin' nobody," says the Lord.
23.33: "So if the people—or a prophet or a priest—ask you, 'What's the oracle of the Lord?' You tell them: 'What oracle? The Lord said He done with y'all.'"
23.34: "And anybody—prophet, priest, or people— Who keep sayin' 'the oracle of the Lord,' I'ma deal with them and their whole household."
23.35: Instead, folks should ask each other, 'What's the Lord sayin' to you?' 'What's the message He gave?'
23.36: Don't say 'the oracle of the Lord' no more. Y'all twisted My words And tried to turn My truth into your own foolish talk.
23.37: So if you wanna know the real deal, Ask, 'What did the Lord answer you?' Or 'What did the Lord say?'
23.38: But since y'all love to say 'the oracle of the Lord,' Even after I told you not to,
23.39: I'm done. For real. I'ma forget y'all, Throw you and your city outta My presence.
23.40: I'ma put shame on y'all name forever. A disgrace that never gets erased."

24.1: The Lord gave me a vision—two baskets of figs sittin' in front of the temple. This was after King Nebuchadnezzar snatched up Jeconiah, the nobles, and the skilled workers from Jerusalem and hauled them off to Babylon.
24.2: One basket had some real good figs—like early season, fresh-picked sweet ones. The other basket? Trash. So rotten they couldn't even be eaten.
24.3: The Lord said, "Jeremiah, what you see?" I said, "Figs. The good ones real good… but the bad ones? Whew—unbearable."
24.4: Then the Lord hit me with this word:
24.5: "These good figs? That's how I see the ones I let get carried off to Babylon. I sent 'em outta here for they own good. They gon' be alright."
24.6: "I got My eyes on them. I'ma bless 'em. I'ma bring 'em back to this land. I'ma build 'em up, not tear 'em down. Plant 'em deep—ain't nobody uprootin' them."
24.7: "I'ma give them a new heart— A heart that really knows Me. They gon' be My people, and I'ma be they God. They gon' come back to Me with everything they got."
24.8: "Now them bad figs? The ones you can't even eat? That's how I feel about Zedekiah, his boys, the leftovers in Jerusalem, And them folks tryna hide out in Egypt."
24.9: "I'ma make 'em an example— A straight-up warning, a curse, a punchline, In every place I scatter 'em. Folks gon' be like, 'Don't end up like them.'"
24.10: "And I'ma send the sword, the famine, and disease Until they wiped off the land I gave their ancestors."

25.1: This the word God gave Jeremiah 'bout all Judah, In the fourth year of Jehoiakim's reign— That's also year one for King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon.
25.2: Jeremiah spoke this to everybody in Judah and Jerusalem.
25.3: He said, "I been preachin' for 23 years straight— Since Josiah's thirteenth year—and y'all still ain't listenin'."
25.4: "God sent prophet after prophet, Wakin' y'all up early with warnings, But you stayed sleep."
25.5: "They all said the same thing: 'Turn from y'all evil ways. Stop doin' dirty. Then you can stay in the land God gave your people.'"
25.6: "They said, 'Don't chase after other gods. Don't provoke God with them idols you made. If you stop, He won't bring harm.'"
25.7: "But nah, y'all didn't listen. And now y'all done brought this heat on yourselves."
25.8: So God says, "Since y'all ain't listenin' to Me—
25.9: I'm bringin' Nebuchadnezzar—yeah, My servant— And all them nations from the north. They gon' wreck this place, Turn it into a horror story, a punchline, a ghost town."
25.10: "No more laughter, No more weddings, No more grindin' grain or lightin' lamps. It's gon' be dark and quiet."
25.11: "This whole land? Desolate. Judah and the surrounding nations Gon' serve Babylon for seventy years."
25.12: "Then after seventy years up, I'm comin' for Babylon too. They gon' get theirs. I'ma make they land just as wrecked."
25.13: "Everything I said 'bout Babylon gon' come true— Every prophecy in this book, All them words I had Jeremiah speak on the nations."
25.14: "The tables gon' turn. Babylon gon' serve others too, And I'ma pay 'em back for what they did."
25.15: Then God said to me, "Take this wine cup of My wrath And make every nation I send you to drink from it."
25.16: "They gon' drink it, Stumble like they drunk, And lose their minds— 'Cause of the sword I'm sending through 'em."
25.17: So I took the cup and did what God said— Had each nation sip His fury.
25.18: First up: Jerusalem and Judah— Kings, princes, the whole city. They gon' be a mess. Everybody talkin' bad on 'em.
25.19: Then Egypt—Pharaoh, his crew, and all the people.
25.20: The mixed crowds, Uz, the Philistine kings—Ashkelon, Gaza, Ekron, Ashdod leftovers.
25.22: Tyre, Sidon, and the island kings way off.
25.23: Dedan, Tema, Buz, folks way out on the edge.
25.24: Arabia and all the desert crews.
25.26: All the northern kings, Far and near—every nation on earth. Even Sheshach gon' drink last.
25.27: And I had to tell 'em: "Drink up. Get drunk. Stumble and fall. Y'all ain't gettin' up. The sword is comin'."
25.28: If they refused the cup, I was to tell 'em straight: "Nah, you drinkin' this. No dodgin' it."
25.29: "If I'm bringin' judgment to the city with My name on it, Y'all really think y'all gon' be safe? The sword's comin' for everybody," says the Lord.
25.30: Then God said, "Prophesy loud. Tell 'em: 'God roarin' from heaven— He shoutin' like a lion over His people. He gon' stomp the nations Like folks crushin' grapes in the winepress.'"
25.31: "The whole earth gon' hear it— 'Cause God got beef with all nations. He ain't lettin' nothin slide."
25.32: "Disaster comin' Nation to nation. A whirlwind stirrin' up From every direction."
25.33: "And that day? Bodies everywhere—from one end of the earth to the other. Ain't nobody mournin'. No burials. Just bodies layin' like trash."
25.34: "Cry out, y'all fake shepherds. Roll in the dirt. Your time is up. Y'all gon' fall hard."
25.35: "Ain't no escape. Y'all done led the people wrong— Now y'all in the crosshairs."
25.36: "Listen close— The leaders cryin', the people hurtin', 'Cause God just cleared out their peace."
25.37: "The calm homes? Cut down and gone."
25.38: "God stepped out like a lion from His den. Why? 'Cause the land full of evil, And He fed up."

26.1: At the start of King Jehoiakim's reign (Josiah's son), the Lord gave Jeremiah a word.
26.2: God said, "Go stand in the courtyard of My house and speak to all them folks from Judah that come to worship. Say everything I told you—don't leave out nothing.
26.3: Maybe, just maybe, they'll actually listen and turn from their wicked ways. If they do, I'll call off the disaster I planned to drop on 'em for how they been acting."
26.4: "Tell 'em this too: 'The Lord says—if y'all don't listen to Me, and don't walk in the law I gave y'all,
26.5: and if you keep ignoring the prophets I been sending—day after day, even though y'all ain't tryna hear them—
26.6: then I'ma treat this temple like I did Shiloh, and this whole city gon' be cursed by every nation out there.'"
26.7: So the priests, the prophets, and all the people heard Jeremiah drop this message in God's house.
