51.6: Run, y'all! Get up outta Babylon while you can. Don't get caught up in her mess. This God's moment of payback, and He don't miss.
51.7: Babylon was like a gold cup in God's hand—had the whole world drunk off her foolishness. Now everybody actin' wild.
51.8: Outta nowhere, Babylon done crashed. Cry for her, if you want. Try and heal her with some balm—but it might be too late.
51.9: We tried to fix Babylon, but she ain't wanna change. Let's bounce—go back home. Her judgment reach all the way to the sky.
51.10: The Lord showed up for us. Let's go back to Zion and tell everybody what God done did!
51.11: Sharpen them arrows. Grab your shields. God stirred up the Medes kings to destroy Babylon 'cause they disrespected His temple.
51.12: Put the flag up on Babylon's wall. Guard up. Watchmen posted. Trap set. God already planned this—now He makin' it happen.
51.13: You sittin' pretty by all them waters, with all that money—but your time up. You've been greedy too long.
51.14: God said, 'I swear, I'm gon' fill your city with men like locusts, and they gon' holler war cries all over you.'
51.15: God made the earth with His power, built the world with His wisdom, and stretched out the sky with His mind.
51.16: When He speaks, the heavens rumble. He pulls steam up from the earth, makes the lightning flash, and wind blow out His stash.
51.17: Folks be lookin' dumb—think they smart, but they ain't. Every smith embarrassed 'cause them fake gods they made ain't real.
51.18: Them idols? Worthless. Straight up nonsense. When God's judgment hits, they get wiped out too.
51.19: But our God? He ain't like that. He made everything. Israel belongs to Him. He go by 'The Lord of Heaven's Armies.'
51.20: God said, 'You my battle axe. I use you to wreck nations and tear up kingdoms.'
51.21: 'You break horses and riders, chariots and drivers.'
51.22: 'You smash men and women, old folks and kids, young men and girls.'
51.23: 'You wreck shepherds and their sheep, farmers and oxen, governors and rulers.'
51.24: God said, 'I'ma pay Babylon and everybody in Chaldea back for everything they did to Zion—y'all gon' see it.'
51.25: 'Babylon, you that big destroyin' mountain? I'm comin' for you,' says the Lord. 'I'ma throw you down and burn you up.'
51.26: 'Ain't nobody gon' use you to build nothin'. You gon' be empty and ruined forever.'
51.27: Raise the flag, sound the trumpet, gather the nations—Ararat, Minni, Ashkenaz. Call a commander. Send them horses like a swarm.
51.28: Get the armies ready—Medes and their kings, rulers, and whole territories.
51.29: The whole land gon' shake when God's will hits Babylon. Ain't nobody gon' be livin' there no more.
51.30: Babylon's strong soldiers gave up. They just sittin' in they spots—scared, weak, burnt out. Gates busted. Homes gone.
51.31: Runners passin' messages back and forth to the king—'Yo, the city surrounded!'
51.32: 'They blocked the exits, burnt the reeds, and the soldiers shook.'
51.33: God said, 'Babylon's like wheat on the threshin' floor—it's time to crush her. Her harvest day is comin'.'
51.34: 'Nebuchadnezzar swallowed us whole, chewed us up, spit us out like nothin'. Treated us like a snack.'
51.35: Zion says, 'Let Babylon pay for the pain they caused. Jerusalem say, 'Put our blood on their heads.'
51.36: God said, 'I got you—I'ma fight for you and get justice. I'ma dry up Babylon's sea and springs.'
51.37: 'Babylon gon' be a heap of rubble, a home for wild dogs. Folks gon' see her and hiss. Ain't nobody gon' live there.'
51.38: 'They used to roar like lions—now they ain't got nothin' left.'
51.39: 'I'ma give 'em a big feast, get 'em drunk, let 'em party—and then they gon' fall into a sleep they'll never wake up from.'
51.40: 'I'ma drag 'em down like lambs to the slaughter—like rams and goats headed to die.'
51.41: 'How the mighty Babylon fallin'! The city that folks praised is now nothin' but rubble.'
51.42: 'Like a sea flood, destruction drowned her. Waves covered everything.'
51.43: 'Her towns dried up, straight ghost towns. Ain't nobody walkin' through.'
51.44: 'I'm takin' down Bel, their fake god. Gonna spit out all he stole. Ain't no nations bowin' to him no more. Babylon's wall? Gone.'
51.45: God say, 'My people, get outta there! Save yourselves from the heat of My wrath!'
51.46: Don't be scared by all the rumors. First year it's one thing, then another rumor comes. War gon' break out—rulers fightin' each other.
51.47: God says, 'It's almost time—I'm takin' down every idol in Babylon. The land gon' be ashamed, and bodies gon' be everywhere.'
51.48: 'Heaven and earth gon' celebrate when Babylon fall—her enemies comin' from the north,' says the Lord.
51.49: Just like she made Israel bleed, now the whole world gon' watch Babylon bleed out too.
51.50: If you made it out alive, don't look back! Remember God and keep Jerusalem in your heart.
51.51: We embarrassed. Folks clownin' us 'cause outsiders walked all up in God's temple.
51.52: But God said, 'The day comin'—I'ma wreck them idols, and people gon' be groanin' all across the land.'
51.53: Even if Babylon climb to the sky, or fortify her towers, I'ma send robbers to snatch her up, says the Lord.
51.54: You hear that? That cry from Babylon? That's the sound of her fallin'.
51.55: The Lord shut down her loud mouth. She used to roar, now she drownin' in her own mess.
51.56: The thief comin'—her strong men caught, bows broken. God don't play. He repays for real.
51.57: He said, 'I'ma get her leaders, smart ones, soldiers—everybody—drunk. They gon' sleep and never wake up.'
51.58: God said, 'Them big Babylon walls? Cracked. Gates? Burned. Y'all workin' hard for nothin'—that fire gon' eat it all up.'
51.59: This what Jeremiah told Seraiah, son of Neriah, when he went to Babylon with King Zedekiah in his fourth year. Seraiah was the travel planner.
51.60: Jeremiah wrote all the bad stuff comin' for Babylon in a book—all of it.
51.61: He told Seraiah, 'When you get there and see the city, read this out loud.'
51.62: Then say, 'Lord, You said this city gon' be wiped out. No people, no animals—just empty forever.'
51.63: 'And when you finish readin', tie that scroll to a rock and toss it in the Euphrates.'
51.64: 'Then say, "Babylon gon' sink like this and never get back up from all the destruction God bringin'."' That's it—that's all Jeremiah had to say.

52.1: Zedekiah was twenty-one when he became king, and he ruled in Jerusalem for eleven years. His mama was Hamutal, daughter of Jeremiah from Libnah.
52.2: He did evil in the Lord's sight—just like Jehoiakim had done.
52.3: It all went down 'cause the Lord was done with Jerusalem and Judah. He let it all fall apart, pushed them out His presence. Zedekiah? He thought he was slick and rebelled against Babylon's king.
52.4: In Zedekiah's ninth year, tenth month, tenth day—Nebuchadnezzar and his whole army showed up at Jerusalem. They surrounded the city and built a wall to trap it in.
52.5: The siege dragged on 'til Zedekiah's eleventh year.
52.6: By the fourth month, ninth day, the famine hit hard—ain't no food left for anybody.
52.7: That's when the wall finally broke. The soldiers ran out at night through a gate by the king's garden. Chaldeans were everywhere, but they tried to escape across the plain.
52.8: But Babylon's army chased Zedekiah down and caught him near Jericho. His soldiers? Gone. Scattered.
52.9: They grabbed the king, brought him to Nebuchadnezzar at Riblah in Hamath, and that's where he got judged.
52.10: They made Zedekiah watch his sons get killed. Then they executed all Judah's leaders at Riblah too.
52.11: After that, they gouged out Zedekiah's eyes, chained him in bronze, and dragged him off to Babylon. He stayed locked up 'til the day he died.
52.12: In the fifth month, tenth day—nineteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar's reign—Nebuzaradan, the captain of the guard, rolled up on Jerusalem.
52.13: He set fire to the Lord's temple, the king's house, and every important house in the city. Burned it all down.
52.14: His whole crew tore down the walls surrounding Jerusalem.
52.15: Then Nebuzaradan took more folks captive: the rest of the poor, the ones who had switched sides, and all the skilled workers.
52.16: But he left a few poor folks behind to take care of the vineyards and farms.
52.17: The bronze pillars, the water basin, and the carts in God's house—they broke all that down and took the bronze back to Babylon.
52.18: They snatched up the pots, shovels, trimmers, bowls, spoons—all the bronze gear the priests used.
52.19: Also grabbed the gold and silver: basins, firepans, bowls, pots, lampstands, spoons, cups—everything of value.
52.20: Those two bronze pillars, that huge basin, the twelve bulls under it, and the carts Solomon made? Too much bronze to even measure.
52.21: One of those pillars was 27 feet tall, 18 feet around, 3 inches thick—hollow inside.
52.22: It had a 7½-foot-high bronze cap with netting and pomegranates all around it. The other pillar had the same.
52.23: Ninety-six pomegranates on the sides, one hundred total in the decoration.
52.24: Nebuzaradan arrested Seraiah the high priest, Zephaniah the second priest, and three doorkeepers.
52.25: He also took a military officer, seven of the king's close advisors, the army's top scribe who recruited troops, and sixty regular men still in the city.
52.26: He brought them all to the king of Babylon at Riblah.
52.27: The king had them executed right there in Hamath. That's how Judah got carried off into exile.
52.28: Here's who got taken: In year seven—3,023 Jews.
52.29: In year eighteen—832 more from Jerusalem.
52.30: In year twenty-three—745 more under Nebuzaradan. All together: 4,600 people.
52.31: Now check this—37 years into Jehoiachin's exile, twelfth month, 25th day, Evil-Merodach became king in Babylon. He decided to show Jehoiachin some love and pulled him out of prison.
52.32: He spoke real nice to him and gave him better status than the other captured kings in Babylon.
52.33: Jehoiachin took off the prison clothes, ate at the king's table regularly, and lived that royal life from then on.
52.34: And every single day, he got his food portion from the king—faithfully, until the day he died.
